metadata_exposure.scale: 0 = an eavesdropper learns nothing, 100 = learns everything listed

items.why: packet sizes and timing reveal what the tunnel is used for, even though the payload is encrypted
extra inner IP header changes every packet size
padding granularity (CBC vs AEAD) shows in the packet lengths
ESP does not hide packet lengths unless padding is added
packet times and byte counts are visible on the wire
outer IP addresses are always in clear; tunnel mode hides the real endpoints behind the gateways

metadata_exposure.note: IPsec cannot hide timing, volume or outer addresses; padding and dummy traffic reduce the traffic-type leak (see the defence simulation).

compliance.label: Guideline mapping against published guidance - NOT a certification or audit result

checks.requirement: Three-key TDEA (3DES) is not acceptable for encryption after 2023
Use an approved block cipher (AES) and mode
Key establishment with at least 112 bits of security strength (finite-field DH of at least 2048 bits)
checks.evidence: Group 19 (256-bit random ECP) provides at least 112 bits

checks.requirement: ESP encryption algorithm is one of the mandatory-to-implement AES-CBC or AES-GCM-16
IKEv2 MODP group 14 (2048-bit) is a mandatory-to-implement group
checks.evidence: only evaluated when group 14 is the negotiated group

not_evaluated: NIST SP 800-77 Rev. 1 (Guide to IPsec VPNs): used as general background only; no individual requirement is encoded here.
RFC 8247 is encoded for one item only (IKEv2 group 14); other group requirement levels are not evaluated.
FIPS 140 module validation, key management, authentication strength and certificate policy are outside what a capture can show.

assessment.cap_rule: score <= 35 + 65 x completeness (LOW needs a score of at least 80, i.e. completeness of at least 69%)

items.title: Verify that Perfect Forward Secrecy is enabled
items.action: PFS is negotiated inside encrypted IKE messages and cannot be seen in a capture. Confirm the ESP proposal contains a DH group (for strongSwan: esp=...-ecp384!) with `ipsec statusall`.

items.title: Capture from before the tunnel comes up
items.action: Start the capture, then bring the tunnel up (for example `tcpdump -w` first, then `ipsec up`), so IKE_SA_INIT is included.
items.why: It is the only place the cipher and DH group are visible; without it the assessment stays incomplete.

items.title: Reduce the traffic-type leak
items.action: An eavesdropper can tell this traffic is web browsing (100%). Padding packets to fixed sizes and adding dummy traffic reduces this; see the defence simulation for the effect measured on this project's dataset.
items.why: IPsec encrypts payloads but not packet sizes or timing.
items.config_hint: (not an ipsec.conf option - needs padding support, e.g. ESP TFC padding, or an overlay)

items.title: Set and verify a short SA lifetime
items.action: Set keylife=1h and ikelifetime=4h, then verify with a capture at least twice as long as keylife so a rekey is observed.
items.why: The lifetime cannot be observed unless a rekey happens inside the capture.

secure_config.text:
# Generated by the IPsec VPN Analyzer - a starting point, NOT a tested production config.
# Replace the <placeholders>, then test in a lab (ipsec statusall, tcpdump) before using it.
config setup
    charondebug="ike 1, esp 1"

conn secure-vpn
    keyexchange=ikev2
    left=<THIS_GATEWAY_IP>
    right=<PEER_GATEWAY_IP>
    type=tunnel
    authby=pubkey                 # certificates; if you must use a pre-shared key: authby=secret with 20+ random characters
    leftcert=<THIS_GATEWAY_CERT>
    ike=aes256gcm16-prfsha384-ecp384!             # AES-256-GCM, SHA-384 PRF, ECP-384 (group 20)
    esp=aes256gcm16-ecp384!             # AES-256-GCM; the ecp384 group here enables Perfect Forward Secrecy
    ikelifetime=4h
    keylife=1h
    rekeymargin=9m
    dpdaction=restart
    dpddelay=30s
    auto=start
secure_config.note: Standard strongSwan syntax, but NOT verified against a running strongSwan in this project (Docker was unavailable). Test it in a lab first; replace every <placeholder>.

cipher_family.evidence: packet lengths fall into 3 different residue classes mod 16 {0: 66, 4: 21, 8: 128}; 16-byte-block CBC cannot produce that (one SA assumed)

integrity_tag.evidence: not observable from packet sizes for this stream (for AEAD ciphers the 8/12/16-byte tag does not change the 4-byte alignment)

mode.evidence: learned from packet-size statistics (tunnel mode adds an inner IP header to every packet); trained on scripted lab traffic

not_observable: AES-128 vs AES-256 (key length does not change packet sizes)
Diffie-Hellman group (only visible in the cleartext IKE_SA_INIT)
Perfect Forward Secrecy (negotiated inside encrypted IKE messages)
Authentication method (pre-shared key vs certificate: encrypted IKE_AUTH)
esp_fingerprint.method: packet sizes only (no file names, no keys, no IKE)

replay_protection.evidence: all 2 SA(s) with enough packets use a strictly increasing sequence counter (no duplicates, no out-of-order packets, 0 sequence numbers never seen)
limits: Whether the receiver enforces the anti-replay window (and its size) is a receiver-side setting and is not observable.
Only the sender's sequence counter can be checked; a capture point can also see duplicates/reordering that never reached the receiver.
The configured SA lifetime is not observable; only the interval between successive SAs seen in this capture.

sa_lifetime.note: not observable in this capture (no rekey - a new SPI in the same direction - was seen)

caveats: Feature-level simulation on scripted lab traffic: real padding/dummy-traffic implementations differ in detail.
The adaptive attacker uses the same 12 window features; a stronger attacker (sequence models, longer windows) may do better.
Captures are short (file transfer, VoIP and video < 2 s), which limits how well dummy traffic and shaping can be judged.
Costs are per capture and depend on how busy the capture is: padding a ping stream costs a lot, padding a bulk transfer almost nothing.
